companyDossiers.name: ABILITY Neurotech

origin.detail: The Wyss project ran from 2018 to 2025 and spun out as a company in March2025. The company separately credits John Donoghue’s earlier Wyss-era vision; this is not a statement that he founded the company.

labRoots.detail: Wyss Center, Geneva, supplied the engineering program; its partners included clinical, university and industrial groups.

precursor.detail: The 2022 platform packaged neural amplification, hermetic feedthroughs, induction power and optical data transmission; it accepted either microelectrode arrays or ECoG grids.

whatChanged.detail: Company translation emphasizes an ECoG speech application and an integrated implant–wearable–decoder system. Surface sensing is a selected application of the platform, not proof of intracortical-array descent.

milestones.title: Wyss ABILITY program
milestones.detail: The institutional project page records the research program and company transition.

milestones.title: Preclinical MEA and ECoG acquisition
milestones.detail: Wyss reports separate sheep studies using penetrating arrays and surface grids with optical telemetry.

milestones.title: Company spinout
milestones.detail: ABILITY Neurotech becomes the independent translation company.

milestones.title: First human acquisition announced
milestones.detail: Initial intraoperative signal acquisition at TUM is performed under general anesthesia.

limits: This is a verified subset of founders. Historical reports name Jonas Zimmermann, but the current inspected company team no longer lists him; no current role is assigned.
The earlier wired locked-in communication case cited by Wyss is not treated here as a clinical trial of the wireless ABILITY implant.
The July2026 acquisition report and future chronic implantation plans are distinct.
The company lists 128channels, 2kS/s ECoG configuration with higher configurable sampling, and50Mbps link capacity; these are specifications, not a claim of 128neurons or achieved speech performance.

companyDossiers.name: Newronika

origin.detail: Founded in2009 by a multidisciplinary team led by Priori, with the University of Milan and Policlinico as participating research institutions.

labRoots.detail: University of Milan and Policlinico neurophysiology/neurotechnology teams supplied clinical and engineering roots.

precursor.detail: FilterDBS addressed stimulation artifacts that obscure small local field potentials; a later portable external system enabled LFP-feedback experiments.

whatChanged.detail: AlphaDBS moves sensing and the feedback algorithm into the implanted pulse generator. Later development adds a clinician-facing data platform and commercial adaptive-system packaging.

milestones.title: FilterDBS publication
milestones.detail: Researchers demonstrate LFP recording during stimulation using an external artifact-suppression system.

milestones.title: Company founded
milestones.detail: Primary company release identifies a multidisciplinary team with university and hospital participation.

milestones.title: Portable adaptive DBS prototype
milestones.detail: An external device combines stimulation and LFP sensing for clinical feedback research.

milestones.title: Implant architecture published
milestones.detail: The implant paper reports sensing data from the first three participants; comparative clinical outcomes remain for the ongoing trial.

milestones.title: Updated adaptive version and data integration
milestones.detail: Company announces a CE-marked commercial version integrated with WebBioBank.

limits: The founder list is a verified subset: current roles do not establish all original founders.
The2021 report’s sixteen stimulation contacts must not be confused with its two differential sensing channels.
The controller described in2021 runs in implant firmware; cloud data management does not imply cloud-based real-time control.
The2022 paper is a trial protocol, not an outcome report.
Company-reported2026 certification is a version-specific milestone; the independent certificate was not inspected and US FDA approval is not claimed.
A current company landing page labels its pilot comparison results pending publication; those marketing percentages are not used here.

integrationNotes: ABILITY’s preclinical Utah-array compatibility is not a corporate Blackrock/BrainGate spinout or licence. Its current speech implant uses ECoG.
ABILITY’s July2026 first-human announcement concerns intraoperative signal acquisition; do not turn it into a completed chronic speech-restoration trial.
For Newronika, stimulation contacts, differential sensing channels, signal sampling and stored spectral summaries are different quantities.
The 2021 AlphaDBS paper describes conventional DBS/sensing CE marking; the 2026 announcement concerns a later adaptive commercial version. Neither implies US FDA approval.
